title: Best ACT practice tests in 2026: official questions, ranked and compared
summary: Compare the best ACT practice tests for 2026: Acely, built with official ACT® questions, the official ACT site, Khan Academy, and Kaplan.
body_markdown:
Use ACT.org for full-length tests made entirely from official ACT questions. Then use Acely for more practice: its library includes 20 full-length ACT tests that combine official ACT questions with educator-crafted Acely questions, plus a 6,000-question bank and detailed pacing analytics.


Acely also turns your results into a dynamic study plan geared toward your areas for improvement. The plan automatically updates as you take tests and study, while the AI tutor provides dynamic hints and explanations when you need help. ACT.org's tests are valuable checkpoints, but they don't include that adaptive study experience.


Yes.[ACT provides four free official full-length practice tests](https://www.act.org/content/act/en/products-and-services/the-act/test-preparation/free-act-test-prep.html) in digital and downloadable paper formats. These are valuable for experiencing official questions and establishing a baseline, but they don't create a personalized study plan from your results.


Acely also offers one free ACT practice test with no credit card required, plus a short skills assessment. Acely's tests combine some official ACT questions with educator-crafted Acely questions. With 20 full-length ACT practice tests available on the full platform, students can continue with realistic practice after working through the four tests on ACT.org.


Your Acely results also feed into a dynamic study plan geared toward your areas for improvement, and that plan updates automatically after every test.


[ACT provides four free official full-length practice tests](https://www.act.org/content/act/en/products-and-services/the-act/test-preparation/free-act-test-prep.html) for the Enhanced ACT. Each is available in a digital format and as a downloadable paper booklet. Because the supply of official material for the current format is limited, students who practice consistently usually need additional realistic tests.


Acely supplements official ACT resources with 20 full-length ACT practice tests and 6,000 questions, including official ACT content and educator-crafted material.


No. Khan Academy focuses exclusively on SAT prep through its partnership with the College Board and does not offer any ACT content. Acely includes full ACT prep with 20 practice tests, 6,000 questions, automated scoring, and a personalized study plan, all in a single subscription alongside SAT prep. Students who are unsure which test to take can practice both on Acely and compare their results. If you're comparing the SAT and ACT, see our[SAT vs ACT guide](https://acely.com/where-to-start/sat-vs-act) to understand more about the differences.


Most students benefit from taking more full-length tests than the official ACT site provides because repeated, timed practice builds familiarity, pacing, and stamina. A useful cadence is one full-length test every two to four weeks, with targeted practice and review between tests.


Avoid taking tests back-to-back without studying your results. Review every missed question, identify whether the issue was content, timing, or a misread, and address those weak areas before the next exam.


The best option combines realistic ACT content with enough practice volume and useful feedback. Acely includes 20 full-length ACT practice tests, 6,000 questions, official ACT content, per-question pacing analytics, and a personalized study plan that updates as you improve.


The official ACT site is also essential for authentic diagnostic tests, but it offers less practice volume and less guidance on what to study next.


Start with the free tests on the official ACT site. When you need more current, full-length practice, Acely offers 20 ACT practice tests and a 6,000-question bank that combines official ACT content with educator-crafted material.


Acely also provides detailed score reports, pacing analytics, and targeted practice between tests, so each full-length exam informs what you study next. Learn more about[ACT prep on Acely](https://acely.com/act-prep) .


Yes. As a preferred ACT® test prep provider, Acely includes official ACT questions in its practice tests, question bank, and personalized study plans, updated for the 2026 enhanced format. Learn more in[Acely's ACT launch announcement](https://acely.com/blog/acely-act-official-partnership) .


Generally, yes. Acely's plans range from $49 to $149 per month based on the selected term and are billed upfront: $588 annually, $297 quarterly, or $149 monthly. Kaplan's guided ACT options cost $649 for Live Online and $849 for tutoring. Kaplan also offers a $179 self-paced course, but Acely includes more full-length practice tests, a larger question bank, detailed pacing analytics, and a 24/7 AI tutor.


Acely also offers a free full-length ACT practice test with no credit card required, so you can try the platform before selecting a paid plan. See[Acely pricing](https://acely.com/pricing) for current plan details.
